items.q: Are my files kept private?
items.a: Yes. All file uploads and downloads are protected with HTTPS encryption in transit. Your files are processed on our secure servers and never read, shared with third parties, sold, or used to train AI models. We have no interest in the content of your files.

items.q: When are my uploaded files deleted?
items.a: All uploaded files and conversion outputs are automatically and permanently deleted within 30 minutes of upload. This applies to both the original file and the processed result. This deletion policy cannot be extended or paused — it is a core privacy feature, not a configurable option.

items.q: Do you store any data about me?
items.a: We do not store personal information. We collect anonymous, aggregated usage statistics (page views, tool usage counts) via standard web analytics. No account, email, or identity is ever linked to a job or a file.

items.q: What is the maximum file size?
items.a: Free users can upload files up to 20 MB. A one-time Pro token ($5, valid for 30 days) raises the limit to 50 MB. No account is required for either option.

items.q: What file formats are supported?
items.a:
PDF tools: .pdf
Image tools: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .webp, .heic, .gif, .bmp, .tiff, .svg
Audio tools: .mp3, .wav, .m4a, .ogg, .flac, .aac, .aiff
Video tools: .mp4, .mov, .mkv, .avi, .webm
Document tools: .docx, .doc, .pptx, .ppt, .xlsx, .xls, .csv, .json, .md, .html

items.q: How does PDF compression work?
items.a: PDF compression reduces the quality and resolution of embedded images, removes redundant data, strips metadata, and optimises the internal structure. PDFWorks offers three quality levels: Low achieves maximum compression but may reduce image sharpness; Medium (recommended) balances file size with visual quality; High preserves maximum quality with modest reduction. PDFs that are mostly text compress less dramatically than image-heavy files.

items.q: What is the difference between a user password and an owner password?
items.a:
A user password (open password) is cryptographically enforced — the file cannot be opened or read without it. PDFWorks uses AES-256 encryption for user passwords.

An owner password controls permissions such as printing, copying, and editing. It is not cryptographically enforced and can be bypassed by most PDF readers and free tools. Do not rely on an owner password to prevent access to the content — use a user password for that.

items.q: I forgot my PDF password. Can PDFWorks recover it?
items.a: No. If you have lost the user (open) password, the content is not recoverable through PDFWorks. AES-256 encryption is strong enough that brute-force recovery of a good password is not feasible. If the file had only an owner (permissions) password and no open password, the Unlock PDF tool can remove it.

items.q: Does flattening a PDF redact sensitive content?
items.a:
No — and this is a common, dangerous misconception.
Flattening converts interactive elements (form fields, annotations, drawn shapes) into static page content. It does not delete any underlying text or images. If you have drawn black boxes over text to "redact" it, the text is still in the file after flattening. Anyone can recover it by removing the annotation layer or extracting the text stream with free tools.

True redaction requires a tool that permanently deletes the underlying content (such as Adobe Acrobat Pro's Redact feature), followed by flattening, followed by verifying the text is no longer selectable.

items.q: What metadata does "Strip Metadata" remove from PDFs?
items.a:
From PDFs: author name, creation date, modification date, application name (e.g. "Microsoft Word 2019"), operating system info, and custom properties.
From images: EXIF data including GPS coordinates, camera make and model, date taken, photographer name, copyright strings, and thumbnail previews.
From audio files: ID3 tags including artist, album, title, year, genre, and embedded artwork.

items.q: Can I convert a scanned PDF to Word?
items.a: It depends. If your PDF was created digitally (from Word, a browser, etc.) it contains actual text and converts accurately. If it is a scanned image of a physical document, the text is embedded as an image and requires OCR first. Use the Document → OCR tool to extract text from scanned images. For best results, ensure the scan is at least 300 DPI and the text is clearly legible.

items.q: Why isn't PDF-to-Word conversion perfect?
items.a: PDF is a fixed-layout format that stores the final visual result, not document structure or style intent. Converting back to an editable format involves reverse-engineering the original layout. Complex documents with columns, tables, or unusual fonts may lose some formatting. Use original Word or editable PDF source files where possible, and expect some manual cleanup after conversion.

items.q: Can I merge multiple PDF files?
items.a: Yes. Go to PDF Tools and select "Merge PDFs". You can upload multiple PDF files at once and the tool will combine them into a single PDF in the order you upload them. All original pages from each source document are retained.

items.q: Which audio formats are supported?
items.a: PDFWorks supports MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, AAC, M4A, and AIFF for both input and output. You can convert between any of these, compress, trim, normalize loudness, change playback speed, or extract audio from a video file.

items.q: Does changing audio speed affect pitch?
items.a: No. The Change Speed tool uses time-stretching (ffmpeg's atempo filter), which adjusts playback duration without altering pitch. A podcast sped up to 1.5× will play faster but will not sound higher-pitched.

items.q: What does "compress WAV" actually do?
items.a: WAV is uncompressed PCM audio — there is no such thing as a compressed WAV that stays in WAV format. When you compress a WAV file on PDFWorks, it is transcoded to MP3 at the chosen bitrate, producing a much smaller file. If you need lossless compression, convert to FLAC instead.

items.q: What is audio normalization and when should I use it?
items.a:
Normalization adjusts the overall loudness of an audio file to a target level measured in LUFS (Loudness Units Full Scale). Use it when:
  • You have recordings at different volumes and want them consistent
  • You are uploading to a streaming platform and need to hit their loudness target (−14 LUFS for Spotify/YouTube, −16 LUFS for general use, −23 LUFS for broadcast)
PDFWorks uses the EBU R128 loudnorm filter, the industry standard for broadcast and streaming loudness.

items.q: Can I extract audio from a video file?
items.a: Yes. The Extract Audio tool accepts MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, and WebM files and outputs the audio track in your choice of format: MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, AAC, or M4A.

items.q: Which video formats does PDFWorks support?
items.a: Video input accepts MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, and WebM. All video output is produced as H.264/AAC MP4, which plays natively on all major browsers, operating systems, and devices without plugins.

items.q: Why does PDFWorks always output MP4 even if I upload a different format?
items.a: MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio is the universal web-safe format. MKV, AVI, and other containers — or codecs like H.265 and VP9 — cause playback failures on many devices and browsers. Standardising to H.264 MP4 guarantees your output plays everywhere without extra software or conversion on the recipient's side.

items.q: How much does video compression reduce file size?
items.a:
Results vary by source material, but typical ranges:
  • High quality — ~10–20% smaller, visually identical
  • Medium quality — ~40–60% smaller, minor quality trade-off
  • Low quality — ~70–80% smaller, visible quality reduction
Screen recordings and animation compress far better than fast-moving footage such as sport or film.

items.q: Is PDFWorks free to use?
items.a: Yes, PDFWorks is completely free to use. All tools — PDF compression, conversion, merging, image editing, audio conversion, and more — are available at no cost. We cover operating expenses through non-personalised display advertising. There are no watermarks on output files.

items.q: Do I need to create an account?
items.a: No account is required. You can use every tool on PDFWorks without signing up, providing an email address, or logging in. Simply upload your file, process it, and download the result.

items.q: How does the Pro token work?
items.a: The Pro token is a one-time payment of $5 that unlocks higher file size limits (up to 50 MB per file) and removes ads for 30 days. Unlike a subscription, it is a single purchase — there is no recurring billing and no account required. The token is linked to your browser session.

items.q: Does PDFWorks work on mobile?
items.a: Yes. All tools are fully functional on modern mobile browsers (Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android). File upload, processing, and download all work on mobile. Some interactions — such as the rotate PDF page grid with multi-select — work best on desktop with a mouse and keyboard.

items.q: Can I process multiple files at once?
items.a: The Merge PDFs tool accepts multiple files simultaneously. All other tools process one file at a time. Batch processing is on our roadmap. Conversions are fast — typically a few seconds per file — so processing files one by one is practical for small batches.

items.q: Why is my job taking a long time?
items.a: Processing time depends on file size and tool complexity. PDF compression of a 1 MB document completes in seconds. Audio normalization, video re-encoding, and OCR on large files may take up to a minute. The status indicator on each tool page updates automatically — you do not need to refresh.

items.q: Is there an API available for developers?
items.a: An API is not publicly available at this time. If you are interested in API access for business use — for example, to integrate PDFWorks tools into your own application — please contact us to discuss options.

items.q: Where can I get help if a tool fails?
items.a: Use the Contact page to report a problem. Include the file type, approximate file size, and what you were trying to do. We aim to respond within one business day.
